title: Standard valuation worksheet v1 (stage 5): reverse DCF, scenario DCF, twin engine, temperature, sensitivity
body: Every deep dive ends with tools/valuation/worksheet.py (standard library only; runs on the Pi). Input: one JSON of company figures (price, shares, net debt, base-year revenue/EBIT/PAT/FCF, economic NOPAT margin, ROIIC, cost of equity default India 12.5% / US 9.5%, terminal growth 5% / 3%, 10 years) plus bear/base/bull scenarios (growth yr1->yrN, end margin, ROIIC, exit P/E, probability) and a blow-up probability. Model: value-driver DCF, FCF = NOPAT x (1 - g/ROIIC), linear fades, TV = NOPAT(1+tg)(1 - tg/ROIC)/(r - tg). Outputs one Markdown section: (a) reverse DCF - revenue CAGR implied by price, year-1 growth fading to terminal, margin needed, IRR the price offers on the base case, feasibility flag when reinvestment > 100% of NOPAT; (b) scenario DCF -> probability-weighted value, bear downside, 5-yr multiples using stated exit P/E next to the DCF-consistent P/E at year 5 (gap flagged), and P(>=2x/3x/5x), P(<=0.5x), P(blow-up), EV and median 5-yr multiple via lognormal spread per scenario; (c) twin-engine EPS CAGR needed for 2x/3x/5x at each exit P/E and the re-rating share; (d) temperature vs own P/E history (n>=5), sector median and Nifty bands; (e) CoE x growth and TG x margin sensitivity. Rules: use economic margins (pre-Ind AS 116, core ex other income, after SBC, adjusted for one-offs); leases out of net debt when rent is in the margin; every input source-tagged or [EST] with method. Guide: research_notes/Templates/valuation_and_decision.md.

data.temp_bands: <0.7 cold, 0.7-0.9 cool, 0.9-1.1 normal, 1.1-1.5 warm, 1.5-2 hot, >=2 very hot

title: Decision card v1 (stage 6): gates from stages 2-5, probabilities vs base rates, written sizing rule, auto paper calls
body: tools/decision/decision_card.py fills tools/decision/decision_card.md from one card JSON that points at the worksheet input. Fields: one-line thesis; variant view; what the price implies; stage-2 hard rules (pass/fail/unknown) and graded flags; stage-3 signals (PEAD avoid flag = SUE quintile 1-2 within ~63 trading days, L19; promise credibility shown sector-adjusted only with a peer median, L18; detector alerts); stage-4 soft flags and override log; P(>=3x/5y), P(<=0.5x), P(blow-up) beside a base-rate class from tools/decision/base_rates.json (null = n/a, never borrowed); EV of the 5-yr multiple vs the index hurdle; position size; dated kill criteria; pre-mortem; review date; gate log. Blocking gates (size 0): any hard rule failed (no override) or unknown (incomplete); PEAD avoid flag active; >=3 open soft flags without a written variant view; EV below hurdle; kill criteria missing/undated. Informational: outside-view check when model P is >2x or <0.5x the base rate. Sizing rule: min(0.25 x Kelly f*, tier cap at cost core 5% / satellite 4% / speculative 2%, liquidity cap adv_pct x ADV x days_to_exit / portfolio); f* maximises E[ln(1+f(M/H-1))] over scenario outcomes vs the hurdle multiple H. Emits three 5-yr paper calls (>=3x, <=0.5x, blow-up) and a decision record in memdb seed format with entry price, resolve_by and a mechanical resolution rule. Phase A: all sizes are paper sizes; practice cards say 'no verdict' and are tagged practice-example.

gates_blocking: >=3 open soft flags and no variant view

title: At India CoE 12-13% a DCF calls almost every 40-50x compounder 60-70% overvalued; read the implied IRR and the exit-multiple gap instead
body: Worksheet v1 on three practice companies (test material, no verdict). With cost of equity 12.5%, terminal growth 5% and terminal ROIC 25-30%, the terminal value is worth ~11-15x NOPAT ((1 - tg/ROIC)/(r - tg) ~ 0.8/0.075 ~ 10.7x at 25% ROIC), so DCF-consistent P/Es at year 5 came out at 12-17x while VMM and Cummins trade at 48-52x: probability-weighted DCF values were -65% and -69% vs price. The informative outputs were (1) the reverse DCF: the price needs ~30% revenue CAGR for 10 years at today's margins, and the path needs reinvestment above 100% of NOPAT at the assumed ROIIC (feasibility flag); (2) the IRR the price offers if the base case happens: 7-8% vs a 12.5% hurdle; (3) the exit-multiple gap: every Indian scenario's stated exit P/E (25-50) was 2-3x its DCF-consistent P/E, i.e., the 5-year return depends on the market continuing to pay high multiples. Rule: for Indian high-P/E names, report implied IRR and the exit-multiple gap, never 'DCF value -65%' as a target; the decision gate uses the 5-year multiple vs the index hurdle. Caveat: the base-rate class used alongside (2020-25 NSE survivors, x3 44%) is bull- and survivor-biased.
